title: Scheme Veronese quotient data and normalized representation interface
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $Z$ an $S$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a commutative unital quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], presented by its graded section algebras on affine opens as in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, define a datum to consist of $d>0$, an $S$-map $f:T\to Z$, an invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], and degreewise $\mathcal O_T$-linear maps $f^*\mathcal A_{dn}\to L^{\otimes n}$ preserving the unit and all products. Tensor products and powers are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; the unit power is $\mathcal O_T$. Use tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Require the degree-one map to be a sheaf surjection. Equivalently, by tensor-pullback adjunction and quasi-coherence, specify restriction-compatible $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$-semilinear additive maps $\mathcal A(V)_{dn}\to\Gamma(f^{-1}V,L^{\otimes n})$ for all affine $V\subset Z$, preserving unit and homogeneous products; their degree-one images locally generate $L$. Two data are related when their maps $f$ agree and for positive $k,l$ with $dk=d'l$ there is $\beta:L^{\otimes k}\simeq(L')^{\otimes l}$ whose $n$th tensor power identifies the two maps in degree $dkn=d'ln$, for every $n\geq0$. Denote the quotient by the equivalence relation generated by these identifications by $C(T)$. Define the graph of pullback along $u:T'\to T$ on data by $d'=d$, $f'=fu$, and an isomorphism $u^*L\simeq L'$ carrying every $u^*\psi_n$ to $\psi'_n$ under the fixed tensor-power comparisons [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison]; define its graph on $C$ by representatives. For arbitrary $T$, define $Q(T)$ to be compatible families of elements of $C(V)$ indexed by quasi-compact open $V\subset T$, compatibility meaning this pullback graph for every open inclusion. Define its top-component evaluation for quasi-compact $T$. A family remembers $f:T\to Z$ when each component has a representative with structural map $f|_V$. A base-linear graded algebra isomorphism $e:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$ acts on quotient classes by representatives whose line is unchanged up to isomorphism and whose homogeneous maps are precomposed by $f^*e_{dn}$. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal A)$ with its specified structural map [def-nagata-relative-proj], and use the ordinary contravariant isomorphism of [def-sfb-relative-proj-iso-of-graded-iso]. Define a normalized representation of this datum to be a set-valued contravariant functor $F$ on $S$-schemes, componentwise bijections $F(T)\simeq Q(T)$ and a natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Mor}_S(-,P)\simeq F$, subject to the following properties: the displayed common-power relation is an equivalence relation; the pullback graph on $C$ is total and single-valued; top-component evaluation is bijective for quasi-compact tests; the maps of $F$ induce the specified pullback graph on every pair of quasi-compact opens through which the test morphism restricts; the representing family of $g:T\to P$ remembers $\pi g$. Finally normalize it against the actual twisting sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]: if a quasi-compact open $W\subset T$ maps through an affine-base chart $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(V))$, every representative $(d,f,L,\psi)$ of its component has, in every degree $n$, an isomorphism $L^{\otimes n}\simeq g|_W^*\mathcal O(dn)$ carrying $\psi_n(b)$ to the pulled-back canonical homogeneous section $b/1$. This defines the objects, relations, compatible-family set and the predicate/data of a normalized representation; it does not assert that such a representation exists.
